**Select the most appropriate word to substitute the underlined word of the given sentence. If substitution is not required select ‘No improvement’.**

To fight on the battlefield for the sake of one's country needs __a great strongness.__
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 2.**

**A great strongness** is an incorrect phrase. It must be replaced with **great courage.**

__
 
• **Strong:** having the power to move heavy weights or perform other physically demanding tasks; powerful, muscular
 
• **Courage:** the ability to do something that frightens one; bravery.

When one fights for the country, one shows courage, not strength.

questions.question:
**Select the correct active form of the given sentence.**

This beautiful story was written by Maya.

options.text: Maya is writing this beautiful story.
Maya was writing this beautiful story.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Maya wrote this beautiful story**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In Active Voice, a sentence emphasizes the subject, performing an action.
 
• In Passive Voice, a sentence emphasizes the action or the object of the sentence.
 
• The given sentence is in the passive voice and '**This beautiful story**' is the subject and '**Maya**' is the object.
 
• When we convert this sentence into active voice, the subject '**This beautiful story**' of the passive voice becomes the object, the object '**Maya**' becomes the subject.
 
• The passive format "was + V3 (written)" should be changed into the active format "V2 (wrote)".
 
• This is the active and passive voice rule for the past simple tense.
 
• Hence, the correct answer is option 1.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

questions.question:
**Select the correct direct form of the given sentence.**

The teacher commanded the students not to shout.

options.text: The teacher said to the students, "Don’t shout.”
The teacher said to the student, "You should not shout.”
The teacher told to the students, "You must not shout.”
The teacher says to the students, "Do not shout."

questions.solution:
The correct direct form of the given sentence, which is in indirect speech, is** option 1) "The teacher said to the students, 'Don't shout."**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• In indirect speech, the speaker's original words are reported by another person, usually with some changes to verb tenses, pronouns, and other elements.
 
• Let's analyze each option to determine the correct one:
 
• **The teacher said to the students, "Don’t shout.”**
 
 
• This option correctly reports the teacher's command by using the reporting verb "said" and enclosing the command within quotation marks.
 
• The contraction "Don't" represents "do not," which is a common way to express prohibition.
 
• The verb tense is also changed from the present tense "commanded" to the past tense "said."
 
• Hence, option 1) is the correct answer.
 
 
 
• **The teacher said to the student, "You should not shout.”**
 
 
• This option changes the subject from "students" to "student," which alters the original meaning. It also replaces "commanded" with "should not," which changes the tone from a direct command to a suggestion or advice.
 
• Therefore, this option does not accurately report the teacher's command.
 
 
 
• **The teacher told to the students, "You must not shout.”**
 
 
• This option replaces the reporting verb "said" with "told to," which is not commonly used in this context.
 
• It also uses the modal verb "must" instead of "don't," which changes the emphasis from prohibition to obligation.
 
• The original command is better represented by "don't shout" rather than "must not shout."
 
 
 
• **The teacher says to the students, "Do not shout."**
 
 
• This option uses the present tense "says" instead of the past tense "said," which does not reflect indirect speech.
 
• The original sentence is in past tense, so the reporting verb should also be in the past tense.
 
• Additionally, the direct command "Do not shout" should be enclosed in quotation marks to accurately represent the teacher's words.

questions.question:
**In the sentence identify the segment which contains the grammatical error.**

Saraswati college has maintained its reputation as one of the best college in the country.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**one of the best college**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• **'one of the best colleges' **should be there in place of **'one of the best college'**
 
• The noun following the phrase '**one of the'** is always a plural noun.

 **Example:* ****There are many birds on the tree. One of the birds is red.

 He is one of the soldiers who fight for their country.*

*​ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__***

 
• Use of verbs as singular or plural will entirely depend upon the subject of the statement, i.e. singular verb for singular subject and plural verb for plural subject.

 **Example: **

 
 
• Pistachio is one of the few flavors that **appeal** to me. (**That** acts as the subject for the verb "appeal", and **that** in this sentence refers to **flavors** (plural noun) and thus, appeal (plural verb) is used.)
 
• The alarm is triggered when one of the criminals **tries** to escape. ("**One criminal**" (singular noun) who tries to escape is the subject for the verb "try", and thus *try* becomes **tries** (singular verb).)
 
 

**Thus the correct sentence will be: ***Saraswati college has maintained its reputation as one of the best colleges in the country.*

questions.question:
**Given below are four jumbled sentences. Pick out one of the given options that give their correct order.**

A. Eventually, she overcame adversities and achieved success.

B. She engaged herself in ‘earn while you learn’, finance scheme in her college.

C. She needed financial support to complete her graduation.

D. Rama was a very poor girl.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 2.**

**When we combine the parts of the paragraph, it is important that we maintain a logical flow in the structure.**

__
 
• A sentence cannot start with a pronoun. A pronoun is a word used instead of a noun.__ *Eg: Anne eats ice cream. She also eats cookies.

 She *refers back to *Anne.*

 Thus our paragraph sentence cannot begin from B or C.So they are ruled out.
 
• **Eventually** means in the end; in due course. It is an **adverb.**

 As we look to start the paragraph, it is wrong to use *Eventually* in the beginning.

 Thus A is ruled out as the beginning of the sentence.
 
• However, it comes in the end of the sentence as a concluding statement.
 
• **D **introduces us to the subject of the sentence ***'Rama'*** and that **she was a poor girl**. Thus it is the correct beginning of the sentence.
 
• **C **follows D. It illustrates about Rama that **she needed financial support to complete her graduation.**
 
• **B **follows C. She overcame the financial crunch as **she joined 'earn while you learn' finance scheme.**
 
• **A **gives a fitting conclusion. Because of the financial scheme, **she overcame her adversities.**

Thus the correct order is **DCBA. **The sentence thus follows:

*Rama was a very poor girl. She needed financial support to complete her graduation. She joined 'earn while you learn' financial scheme in her college. Eventually, she overcame adversities and achieved success.*

questions.question:
**Given below are four jumbled sentences. Pick one of the given options that fit in their correct order.**

A. “We are going to the market,” declared Reetu and Geetu.

B. “Where are you going?” the father asked.

C. “Take your umbrella, it is going to rain,” the mother said.

D. “Yes, definitely. We will,” replied the two.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 1.**

From the given sentence, we understand that it is a conversation between mother, father and their two daughters.

**The scrambled parts must be arranged logically to understand their entire conversation. It is important to establish a connection between these parts.**

 
• **Option 2 **as the order suggests DCAB gives a reverse order of the conversation. Line D starts with an affirmative response, without any prior link to the dialogue. The paragraph thus cannot start with D. Thus it is ruled out.
 
• **Option 3 **as we consider, **AB **is an answer to the question followed by the question. This is a reverse order and hence the paragraph cannot start with D. Thus it is ruled out.
 
• The paragraph thus begins with **B. **It is an **introduction to the conversation about 'where the girls are going'.**
 
• **A **follows B. The response to the question is answered in A. It states **'the girls are going to the market'.**
 
• **C **follows A. The mother tells the girls to **carry an umbrella as it is going to rain.**
 
• **D **follows C. It is the daughter's agreement **'yes we will...'** to mother's statement.

Thus the correct order is **BACD.**

*“Where are you going?” the father asked. “We are going to the market,” declared Reetu and Geetu. “Take your umbrella, it is going to rain,” the mother said. “Yes, definitely. We will,” replied the two.*
